n127/README.md and #1015 say the packing has a tilted central band of 57 squares inside a frame of axis-aligned squares; that the search started from an exact certificate of an arrangement in the public Kaggle coordinate compilations of Alex Chilton and Asterios Panoras, whose original finder could not be established, changed the sliding offsets of the columns in the tilted band and then optimized the positions and angles of individual squares; that no test of local optimality was run and no optimality is claimed; and that on the Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard Luka Cvetkovic reported 11.800793726618 at 127 (16 November 2026), 0.0000020 below this packing, with no coordinates found. #1015 asks that the bound be credited to Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology, after the arrangement in the Chilton and Panoras compilations.

verify_exact.py (separating axes) and check_area.py (the area of each close pair's clipped intersection), both Python's fractions.Fraction and its standard library only, are the folder's two exact checkers; #1015 says each reports 127 squares and 311 close pairs, that they share no code but have one author and read the same input file, and that the witness file has not yet been run through this repository's checker. #1015 says the search, optimization and rational certificate were produced with GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) and the repository files, checks and figure with Claude (Anthropic), both under his direction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
